finding: The page states multimodal systems are more robust than single-modality systems.
handling: This is a potential benefit, not an unconditional guarantee for noisy, stale or poorly fused signals.
method: Use explicit supplied failure cases and the later synchronization/engineering requirements rather than assume a universal improvement.

finding: Confidence scores are said to indicate prediction reliability.
handling: A score is a model output, not automatically a calibrated probability of correctness or ground truth about inner emotional state.
method: Distinguish model classification, held-out calibration and latent state; use the actual screenshot as output evidence only.

primaryEvidence.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
primaryEvidence.locator: Confidence and empirical correctness need not agree; calibration is distinct from class prediction.

finding: Audio buffering is said to ensure uninterrupted output and interruptions immediately terminate playback.
handling: Finite buffers cover only bounded delivery gaps; local playback cancellation has implementation and detection latency.
method: Derive a finite-buffer counterexample and separate generation cancellation from queued client audio.

finding: Message passing is said to eliminate direct dependencies between software modules.
handling: It decouples direct function calls, but modules still share topic names, message schemas, QoS compatibility and data meaning.
method: Trace the exact graph and state a replacement-module contract; do not infer dependency-free interchangeability.

finding: Applications include recognizing engagement, confusion, frustration and operator attention.
handling: Those richer states are not themselves among the seven explicitly listed expression outputs; applications need additional inference and validation.
method: Compare the application wording to the seven-category model description without claiming that application research is impossible.
